item: A rollup build that ends in an error keeps a failure hold released like the duckdb-limit hold, so the next request does not start the same build again (R172)
summary: Measured before: a RuntimeError forced in the build, 5 requests, 5 builds, no hold, boot row unknown. Now the failure keeps a hold in THIS process only (reason build-failed, stage or stage_why, exception class, consecutive failures; never the exception text), released by a larger limit, offload allowed, a 5% smaller corpus or another version; a restart retries once and the kept record carries only the run of failures across it, so across a restart a transient error does not keep the accelerator off; WITHIN one process the hold has only those size-based releases, so a transient error (a locked database, say) keeps the accelerator off until one of them or a restart, and every serve in between answers live (a time or backoff release is not built). OPEN, named by the independent read and not built: a time or backoff release for a failure hold; the per-shard checkpoint's non-fatal failures log a traceback each (up to the shard count) and reuse the compact's wording; _bulk_insert's other callers (refresh, meta upsert, read model) now raise the private _PlainEngineWall instead of OutOfMemoryException; _checkpoint reads an InterruptException as a failure it carries on from (nothing interrupts that connection today). two more nits of the delta read are OPEN: decline_detail() with no hold returns reason unknown with a note that calls a verdict-error failure a decline (or returns an older transient skip), and a verdict error after a restart rewrites last_outcome to failed beside a run count carried from the kept record. status()['last_outcome'] changes only when a build ran or failed, so it keeps saying 'failed' while the hold refuses the requests that follow. A build that serves, or ends in a stop of another kind, ends the run. The record's stage is the LAST REPORTED stage, not the raising statement (the key is the one the duckdb-limit hold uses). status() gains last_outcome, consecutive_failures and last_failure_class ONLY while the run is above 0: absent means 0 since the last serve. The boot step row names the class. Plain OOM stays the duckdb-limit stop; the dormant persisted path is not touched. Net bytes: the constant refresh 'change-gated' left status(); worst-case columnar.json rollup_serve row 1,553 B base -> 1,528 B (duckdb-limit hold) and 1,045 B (failure hold), pinned by a test.
